scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc1 (195.11.14.2) has lost all connectivity to the partner AS --
pings to pc2 (200.1.1.2) fail. The partner operator says their
router2 shows the eBGP session to us as down and keeps retrying,
and swears they changed nothing on their side. Our router1 is up
and pc1 can still reach its gateway 195.11.14.1. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the eBGP neighbor statement for router2 from router1's BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 BGP configuration (neighbor statement)
Mechanism: router1's `router bgp 1` section no longer contains
  `neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2`. Deleting the peer tears the
  eBGP session down immediately: router1 loses the learned route
  to 200.1.1.0/24 and stops advertising 195.11.14.0/24, so pc1 and
  pc2 lose each other in both directions. bgpd is still RUNNING on
  router1 (pgrep bgpd is non-empty) and `router bgp 1` with its
  `network 195.11.14.0/24` line is still present -- only the
  neighbor definition is gone. router2 is healthy: its config and
  daemon are intact and it cycles trying to re-establish, because
  router1 no longer has it configured as a peer.
Localization: router1
Root cause: BGP neighbor statement for 193.10.11.2 (remote-as 2)
  missing from router1's configuration
Fix: re-add the neighbor statement on router1 (see [FIX])
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the neighbor on router1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 1" -c "neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2"`
The eBGP session re-establishes and the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged.
(A `service frr restart` on router1 also restores it, since /etc/frr/frr.conf
on disk was never modified.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BGP neighbor statement for 193.10.11.2 missing from router1's config
must-distinguish-from-daemon-down: recognizes bgpd is still running on router1 and the peer is unconfigured, not a crashed daemon or a link failure
bonus-exonerates-router2: notes router2's config/daemon are intact and its session retries fail only because router1 no longer has the peer configured

agent.diagnosis_text:
The eBGP session between AS 1 (router1) and AS 2 (router2) is down because
router1's BGP configuration is entirely missing the neighbor declaration for
router2. Router2 (AS 2) is correctly configured — it has `neighbor 193.10.11.1
remote-as 1` pointing at router1's eth0 address, is advertising 200.1.1.0/24,
and is perpetually in the Active state while it retries TCP connections to
193.10.11.1:179. Router1, however, has no `neighbor` statement at all in its
`router bgp 1` block; vtysh confirms "No BGP neighbors found in VRF default"
and the kernel routing table on router1 contains only its two directly-connected
prefixes — there is no BGP-learned route to 200.1.1.0/24. Because router1's
BGP daemon does not know 193.10.11.2 is a valid peer, it never opens a TCP
session toward router2 and rejects (or simply ignores) router2's inbound
connection attempts. The L3 underlay is fine — both eth0 interfaces share the
193.10.11.0/24 subnet and are up. The fault is purely a missing BGP peer
statement on router1.

Root cause: The `neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2` line was removed from
router1's BGP configuration, leaving it with no configured peers.

Corrective fix: Add the following to router1's FRR configuration and reload:
  router bgp 1
    neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2
This will allow the eBGP session to establish, exchange the 195.11.14.0/24 and
200.1.1.0/24 prefixes, and restore end-to-end reachability between pc1 and pc2.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies router1 as the affected device and attributes the missing neighbor statement to router1's BGP configuration.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: BGP neighbor statement for 193.10.11.2 missing from router1's config
per_axis.rationale: Agent clearly identifies that router1 is missing the `neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2` BGP statement in its configuration.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-from-daemon-down: recognizes bgpd is still running on router1 and the peer is unconfigured, not a crashed daemon or a link failure
per_axis.rationale: The report states the problem is a missing neighbor statement on router1 (vtysh shows no neighbors) and explicitly rules out underlay/link failure, implying bgpd is running and the issue is unconfigured peer rather than a daemon crash.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-router2: notes router2's config/daemon are intact and its session retries fail only because router1 no longer has the peer configured
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router2's daemon/config are intact, that it repeatedly attempts to connect but stays Active, and attributes the failure solely to router1 missing the neighbor statement.
The agent correctly prescribes re-adding neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2 to router1's BGP config (and reloading FRR), which will re-establish the eBGP session and restore routes.

The agent collected router running-configs and BGP summaries; router1's 'show bgp summary' explicitly reported no BGP neighbors while router2's BGP summary showed a peer, and the agent used these observations to attribute loss of routes to a missing neighbor statement on router1. The conclusion follows logically though some supporting outputs (full config/routing table snippets, bgpd process check) were truncated in the log but were solicited.
